name: Jerimoth
title: Levite and Temple Musician
summary: Jerimoth is a name that appears several times in the Old Testament, referring to various individuals in Israel's history. The most prominent Jerimoth was a Levite who served during King Hezekiah's religious reforms and contributed generous gifts to the temple. The name means 'he who fears' or 'exaltations' and is borne by persons associated with temple service and the tribes of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Jerimoth, son of Becher from the tribe of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Jerimoth is mentioned as one of the sons of Becher from the tribe of Benjamin in the genealogies of Chronicles. He was among the brave warriors of his fathers.

keyEvents.title: Jerimoth among David's Warriors
keyEvents.description: A Jerimoth is mentioned among the mighty warriors who joined David in Ziklag when he was fleeing from Saul.

keyEvents.title: Jerimoth, a Levite in David's Time
keyEvents.description: Jerimoth was one of the Levites appointed to play musical instruments when the ark of the covenant was brought to Jerusalem during King David's reign.

keyEvents.title: Jerimoth, son of David
keyEvents.description: One of David's sons was named Jerimoth. His daughter Mahalath married King Rehoboam, Solomon's son.

keyEvents.title: Jerimoth during Hezekiah's reforms
keyEvents.description: During King Hezekiah's great religious reforms, Jerimoth was one of the Levitical overseers responsible for gifts and tithes brought to the temple.

keyEvents.title: Jerimoth among those who had taken foreign wives
keyEvents.description: After the exile, a man named Jerimoth was among those who had taken foreign wives and was required by Ezra to separate from them to maintain covenant purity.
